title: Nsight Compute report (--page raw CSV): replayed kernel counters, off the run clock
evidence: Observed: Nsight Compute replay (each kernel replayed in isolation, caches flushed, base clocks); not on the run clock

tie.run: the kernels-level run (labels.json trace kernels, a profile_range) whose latest earlier timeline-level run of the same rep is this run, with an equal prompt.json
tie.rule: same request prompt and engine iteration; k-th profiled kernel (ncu ID order = launch order) <-> k-th kernel of that iteration on the timeline run, by launch start; accepted only when the kernel short names match
tie.evidence: Inferred: two runs of the same request; launch order and names matched, timing not shared

_sections_doc: trace/kernels.csv (ncu --page raw, written by rep.py) lacks some headline counters; the importer reads those from trace/sections.csv (ncu --page details) by [Section Name, Metric Name]. The details page rounds to two decimals.
_headline_doc: ie-run/3 keeps only these counters per kernel (owner ruling 2026-11-08: ncu is link-only; L6 shows headline counters and opens the report in ncu-ui). keep_metrics and keep_all_numeric serve the ie-run/2 prototype importer only.
headline: gpu__time_duration.sum
sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active
dram__bytes_op_read.sum
dram__bytes_op_write.sum
lts__t_bytes.sum
sm__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed
gpu__compute_memory_throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed
_scale_doc: ncu --page raw CSV prints each column in a display unit (row 2), e.g. us or Mbyte; ie-run/3 scales headline values to the keep_metrics unit. ncu byte prefixes are decimal (L2 bytes in Mbyte times 1e6 are whole 32-byte sectors). The ie-run/2 store kept the display values under the keep_metrics unit.

measures.formula: FLOPs / (DRAM read + DRAM write) per kernel
